sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface biotinylation assay confirmed FLAG-tagged CD320 is present on the cell surface (PMC13382787, L6). N-glycosylation mutants of the FLAG-tagged construct retained surface trafficking, confirming the tag does not disrupt membrane targeting (L4).
sites.rationale: CD320 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a signal peptide spanning residues 1-35; the mature N-terminus begins at residue 36 (S). An N-terminal tag on a protein with a signal peptide must be placed after the SP cleavage site (after residue 35) to avoid being cleaved off with the signal peptide. No clip names a specific junction residue, but exactly one extracellular N-terminus exists, so the position is topology-derived. The tag is 196 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. Surface display was confirmed by biotinylation. Full-length human CD320 expressed with an N-terminal FLAG tag in HEK293 cells (PMC11667166). Surface display confirmed by cell-surface biotinylation and NeutrAvidin pull-down with anti-FLAG western blot (PMC13382787). Multiple independent studies used this construct.

sources.claim: We expressed human CD320 with an N-terminal FLAG tag ( Fig. 1 A ) in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells.
To examine CD320 complex formation, we made another plasmid expressing CD320 with an N-terminal V5 tag.
HEK293 cells transfected with the CD320 cDNA fused to a green fluorescent protein (GFP) in the protein-expression plasmid pEGFP(19).

literature_notes: All three ledger-supported sites map to the same physical junction (insert_after_residue=35, between the signal peptide cleavage site and the mature N-terminus of CD320). They are reported as separate entries because they use distinct tags (FLAG, V5, GFP) from independent publications. No clip names a specific junction residue for any construct, so all positions are topology-derived: CD320 is a type I single-pass TM protein with SP (1-35), extracellular domain (36-230), TM (231-250), and intracellular tail (251-282); the only extracellular terminus is after residue 35. The C-terminal tail (251-282) is intracellular and no clip reports a tag there. Ledger lines L4, L6, L7, L8 corroborate surface display of FLAG-tagged constructs but do not add new junction positions. L7 mentions disease variants E88del and S162A in the extracellular domain, but these are amino-acid substitutions/deletions, not tag insertions, so they do not qualify as sites. N-glycosylation sites Asn126, Asn195, Asn213 (L4) are noted as constraints within the extracellular domain but no tag insertion was reported at those positions.
